Passing options and outlet context

The UGA chapter distinguishes bounce, chest and overhead passes. It describes a bounce pass as reaching a teammate after contacting the floor, with a typical use when defenders have raised hands. A chest pass begins from the chest with both hands on the ball and a forward push from the chest; the chapter associates it with distance or speed. An overhead pass starts above the head and includes a forward follow-through. The chapter presents it as a common outlet option after a rebound, when the rebounder sends the ball to a teammate farther along the court. These are source-described technique and tactical examples.

General introductory basketball reference, selected and paraphrased from the cited chapter. No youth-specific suitability, training dose, medical clearance or planner approval is established.

Source: 2. Fundamentals – Passing, Ch.1 - Basketball, UGA PEDB Program. https://open.online.uga.edu/basketball/chapter/2-fundamentals-passing/
